title: ContinuousCoefficientPullbackIso
statement:
theorem continuousCoefficientPullback_isIso (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u)
    [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian X] [CompactSpace X]
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ X) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion h] :
    letI := coefficientExtensionNormedField l E
    IsIso (continuousCoefficientPullback
      (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)) h) ∧
    IsIso (continuousCoefficientPullback (ULift.{u + 1, u} E) h)

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12; Lemma 6.5.8(1) (integral coefficient restriction); Definition 6.8.1; Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2); paragraph before Definition 6.8.6 (compatibility with locally closed immersions).

proof.text: Use the completion module's pointwise residue cone. The constant-sheaf adjunction makes its canonical constant comparisons invertible. For discrete rings, comparison with continuous functions identifies these comparisons with continuousCoefficientPullback by adjunction. Every positive coefficient ring is finite. The existing finite-tower inverse-image theorem preserves the residue cone, after transporting along the constant/discrete-function diagram isomorphism. The isomorphism between the two limit cones is the canonical integral pullback: applying each residue projection reduces this assertion to coefficient naturality, which is verified by adjunction and pointwise evaluation. This argument works for any scheme morphism; the theorem keeps its original immersion hypotheses.

The normalized localization comparison gives two proved elementary facts: rational sheaf maps are determined by integral numerators, and an integral sheaf map sending the constant uniformizer to a unit extends uniquely to rational coefficients. Construct g from the inverse of integral pullback followed by pullback of the coefficient inclusion. Constant comparisons, natural in the coefficient ring, identify g on constant integral sections with the map from constant field sections into the pulled-back rational sheaf. The uniformizer is nonzero, since it generates the nonzero maximal ideal, so these sections are units. Extend g by the localization universal property. Coefficient naturality shows that its composite with canonical rational pullback is the identity on integral numerators, hence on rational coefficients. The opposite composite is also the identity: the integral-to-rational map is an epimorphism by the same uniqueness, and the inverse-image adjunction preserves epimorphisms. This constructs an inverse to precisely the canonical rational map.

proof_origin.place: Lemmas 6.5.8(1), 6.8.2 and paragraph before Definition 6.8.6; use the existing finite-tower theorem and prove the localization universal property explicitly
